A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe the same Scale Anchoring and Frequency Representation Learning (FRL) study. The main text, six figures, 34 tables, and Appendices A-J can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original frequency-response experiments, fluid simulations, and weather-forecasting evaluations in Sections 3, 4.2, and 6, with additional measurements, ablations, and failure cases in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the main evaluations and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: FRL's multi-resolution data construction, Nyquist-normalized frequency encoding, frequency-aware objective, and inference procedure are unchanged. Section 5 and Algorithm 1 in Appendix C match.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same convection-diffusion simulations, Non-reacting HIT, MegaFlow2D, single-level and multi-level ERA5 forecasting, and channel-flow scenarios at different Reynolds numbers.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same architecture-specific baselines, FNO/PINO fluid comparators, TNO/Climate FNO weather comparators, and alternative frequency encodings in Appendix H. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, preprocessing, training and test resolutions, model configurations, training budgets, rollout procedures, and evaluation metrics are unchanged in Section 6.1 and the appendices.

E4.justification: Both retain the frequency-response diagnostics, computational and memory analyses, component ablations, encoding replacements, hyperparameter sensitivity tests, and high-Reynolds-number failure analysis. Tables 31-33 and Figure 6 address the same questions with the same evidence.

E5.justification: Both specify global seed 42 and, in Appendix B, ten tests per frequency point with different random initializations. No repeated-run information, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and plotted findings match throughout. For example, Table 3 retains FRL RMSERatio values spanning 0.135-0.375, and Table 31 retains the full-FRL average of 0.202. Figure re-embedding does not change the plotted results.

T1.justification: The Scale Anchoring theorems and proofs in Section 4.1 and Appendix A, normalized-frequency error analysis in Appendix D, and complexity derivations in Appendix E are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and closing discussion retain the same claims about Scale Anchoring, FRL's normalized encoding, architecture-independent benefits, and limited overhead. Trimming a background phrase in the introduction does not revise these core claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations of frequency blindness and scale decoupling are unchanged. Both retain the spectral-regularity assumptions, lack of guaranteed numerical-order convergence, high-Reynolds-number failure explanation, and proposed physical spectral constraints.

D1.justification: v2 removes v1's Reproducibility Statement on pages 10-11, including the promise to release code, configurations, checkpoints, data-preparation scripts, and archived commit hashes. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, preprocessing details, and pseudocode remain unchanged. This changes disclosure without establishing any actual change in resource availability.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against neural operators, spectral bias, and discretization mismatch are unchanged. Removing the brief introductory phrase about deep learning potentially replacing numerical methods does not revise FRL's relationship to prior approaches.

P1.justification: v2 updates affiliations and contact information, adds the ICLR 2026 publication header and funding acknowledgements, removes the Reproducibility Statement, and trims one introductory phrase. The scientific narrative and appendix organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 changes the author-block layout, headers, and some spacing. Figures are embedded at different image resolutions, with visibly sharper rendering especially in Figure 6. Figure and table content, captions, and organization are retained.

improvement.justification: The scientific argument, empirical evidence, proofs, and limitations remain unchanged, including the appendices. Sharper figures and updated front matter provide modest presentation benefits. Removing the future artifact-release pledge reduces disclosure, but existing implementation instructions remain and neither PDF provides code/checkpoint access. These limited changes leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
